correctness.rationale: For the plus-sign Chen–Wang normalization used in the rigorous literature, exact differentiation gives \(L(z+xy+x)=a-x^2+4y^2\), hence \(\mathbb E[x^2]=a+4\mathbb E[y^2]\). Arbitrary antiderivative tests give \(\mathbb E[y\mid x]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[z\mid y]=0\). For positive parameter, equality forces \(y=0\) on the invariant support, then \(z=0\), then \(x^2=a\), proving the equilibrium-mixture classification. For negative parameter, equality in the lower RMS bound would force \(x=y=z=0\), where \(\dot z=a\ne0\), so the bound is strict. The packaged checker verifies the nonstandard polynomial identity exactly.

value.rationale: The defining theme of the Chen–Wang model is the transition between zero and two equilibria while chaotic dynamics can persist. The exact identity places that same parameter transition into a global stationary law: on the two-equilibrium side, equilibrium mixtures are the sharp minimum-RMS states and every other compact recurrent component must exceed the equilibrium amplitude; on the no-equilibrium side, any compact recurrence must carry a strictly positive parameter-controlled velocity RMS. This applies to arbitrary compact invariant measures rather than a selected numerical attractor or a single local bifurcation branch, making it a motivated structural complement to the established literature.
